message.content:
Here’s a quick Python snippet that does exactly that:

```python
temp = "hello=good="
parts = temp.split('=', 1)   # split only at the first '='
print(parts)                 # → ['hello', 'good=']
```

`split('=', 1)` tells Python to split on the first `'='` only, so everything after that first separator (including any trailing `=` characters) stays together in the second element.
